# instruction.md

## Report Brief

You are tasked with producing a **trend analysis report** examining 11 years (2015–2025) of BIEK Computer Science 12th Class (HSC Part-2) past examination papers. The audience is **educators and curriculum planners** who need to understand how the exam has evolved — shifts in question types, volume changes year-over-year, and recurring topic patterns — so they can make informed decisions about curriculum alignment and exam preparation strategies.

## Purpose & Motivation

This report should answer a central question: *Has the BIEK Computer Science exam structure remained stable, or have meaningful shifts occurred that educators should respond to?* The findings should be concrete and data-driven, enabling teachers to prioritize topics and question formats that consistently appear, and helping curriculum planners spot gaps or over-represented areas.

## Key Priorities

- **Year-by-year distribution and question type trends are the heart of this report.** Dedicate the strongest analytical depth here — use clear visualizations (line charts, stacked bars) showing how MCQ, Short, and Long question counts shift across years.
- **Topic pattern analysis matters.** Perform keyword/frequency analysis on the question text column to surface recurring concepts. This is where educators extract the most actionable value.
- **The strategic insights section should feel practical**, not generic — tie recommendations directly to the data patterns you uncover.
- Maintain an **analytical, detailed, and educational tone** throughout.

## Critical Data Integrity Rule

**Do NOT fabricate any numbers, trends, or statistics.** Every figure, percentage, and claim must be derived exclusively from `data.csv`. If data is missing or ambiguous for certain years, say so explicitly in the conclusions.

## Output Format

Deliver the final report as **`/app/output/final_report.html`**. Use a clean, professional layout suitable for educators reviewing in a browser. Embed all charts and visualizations inline.

Refer to `task_input.json` for the full specification of required sections, KPIs, and analysis dimensions.

---

## Data Sources

1. Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md` for dataset documentation and column descriptions.
2. Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json` for report requirements, KPIs, and analysis dimensions.
3. Read `/app/benchmark/data.csv` as the primary dataset to analyze.

## Output Requirements

1. Output the final report to `/app/output/`. Use the filename and format specified in the instruction above.
2. All visualizations must be embedded in the report (inline SVG, base64 images, or chart libraries loaded via CDN).
3. The report must be self-contained — openable directly in a browser (if HTML) or readable as-is (if PDF).

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or wait-for-user instructions, make a professional judgment and continue.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies `report.tone`, `report.audience`, etc., use them to choose color schemes, chart types, and layout styles. Otherwise, make professional judgments.
3. **Priority** — these rules override any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The skill's workflow, quality standards, and technical specs remain fully effective — only skip interactive waits.

# BIEK Computer Science 12th Class Past Papers (2015–2025)

## About the Dataset

This dataset is a community-compiled question bank of **Computer Science** examination questions for **12th Class (HSC Part-2 / Intermediate Second Year)** under the **Board of Intermediate Education Karachi (BIEK)**. It was sourced from the Kaggle dataset published by user *sadamumer* and covers examination years from **2015 to 2025**.

The dataset contains **327 rows** and **4 columns**, with each row representing a single examination question. Questions span three types: Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs), Short Questions, and Long Questions.

**Source**: Official past papers published by BIEK (https://www.biek.edu.pk/) and publicly available scanned papers from educational platforms. Questions were manually extracted, typed, and verified for accuracy.

**Scope**: Focuses on Computer Science Paper-II (theory portion). Practical questions and Paper-I content are not included unless they overlap with Paper-II topics.

## File Information

- **File name**: `cs-12th-question-bank-biek-su.csv`
- **Encoding**: UTF-8
- **Total rows**: 327
- **Total columns**: 4

## Column Schema

| Column Name | Type    | Description |
|-------------|---------|-------------|
| `id`        | Integer | Unique identifier for each question (sequential). |
| `year`      | Integer | Year of the BIEK examination (ranges from 2015 to 2025). |
| `type`      | String  | Type of question. Possible values: `"MCQs"`, `"Short"`, `"Long"`. |
| `question`  | String  | The full text of the question. For MCQs, answer options are separated by a `$` delimiter. For Long Questions, multiple sub-parts may also be separated by `$`. |

## Key Column Details

### `year`
Integer values representing the BIEK examination year. The dataset spans 11 years: 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025. Note that some years may include questions from both annual and supplementary examinations, though this distinction is not explicitly encoded in a separate column.

### `type`
A categorical string column with exactly three possible values:
- **MCQs** — Multiple Choice Questions, typically with four options
- **Short** — Short-answer questions requiring brief explanations or definitions
- **Long** — Long-answer or essay-type questions, often with multiple sub-parts

### `question`
Free-text column containing the question content. A special **dollar sign (`$`)** delimiter is used within this field to separate MCQ answer choices or to delineate sub-parts within long questions. When analyzing this column for topic extraction or keyword frequency, the `$` separator should be accounted for during text preprocessing.

## Data Quality Notes

- The dataset is relatively clean with no reported missing values in the core columns.
- The `question` column uses a non-standard `$` delimiter rather than line breaks, which requires parsing logic during text analysis.

# BIEK Computer Science 12th Class Past Papers (2015–2025)

## About the Dataset

This dataset is a community-compiled question bank of **Computer Science** examination questions for **12th Class (HSC Part-2 / Intermediate Second Year)** under the **Board of Intermediate Education Karachi (BIEK)**. It was sourced from the Kaggle dataset published by user *sadamumer* and covers examination years from **2015 to 2025**.

The dataset contains **327 rows** and **4 columns**, with each row representing a single examination question. Questions span three types: Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs), Short Questions, and Long Questions.

**Source**: Official past papers published by BIEK (https://www.biek.edu.pk/) and publicly available scanned papers from educational platforms. Questions were manually extracted, typed, and verified for accuracy.

**Scope**: Focuses on Computer Science Paper-II (theory portion). Practical questions and Paper-I content are not included unless they overlap with Paper-II topics.

## File Information

- **File name**: `cs-12th-question-bank-biek-su.csv`
- **Encoding**: UTF-8
- **Total rows**: 327
- **Total columns**: 4

## Column Schema

| Column Name | Type    | Description |
|-------------|---------|-------------|
| `id`        | Integer | Unique identifier for each question (sequential). |
| `year`      | Integer | Year of the BIEK examination (ranges from 2015 to 2025). |
| `type`      | String  | Type of question. Possible values: `"MCQs"`, `"Short"`, `"Long"`. |
| `question`  | String  | The full text of the question. For MCQs, answer options are separated by a `$` delimiter. For Long Questions, multiple sub-parts may also be separated by `$`. |

## Key Column Details

### `year`
Integer values representing the BIEK examination year. The dataset spans 11 years: 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025. Note that some years may include questions from both annual and supplementary examinations, though this distinction is not explicitly encoded in a separate column.

### `type`
A categorical string column with exactly three possible values:
- **MCQs** — Multiple Choice Questions, typically with four options
- **Short** — Short-answer questions requiring brief explanations or definitions
- **Long** — Long-answer or essay-type questions, often with multiple sub-parts

### `question`
Free-text column containing the question content. A special **dollar sign (`$`)** delimiter is used within this field to separate MCQ answer choices or to delineate sub-parts within long questions. When analyzing this column for topic extraction or keyword frequency, the `$` separator should be accounted for during text preprocessing.

## Data Quality Notes

- The dataset is relatively clean with no reported missing values in the core columns.
- The `question` column uses a non-standard `$` delimiter rather than line breaks, which requires parsing logic during text analysis.
- This is a **non-official, community-compiled dataset** — minor transcription errors may exist.
- The dataset does not distinguish between annual and supplementary examination papers.
- With only 327 rows, this is a compact dataset well-suited for pattern analysis but may have limited statistical power for fine-grained topic-level trend detection.
- All text is in English, consistent with the BIEK Computer Science examination medium.

steps.reasoning_content:
Now I have all the data. Let me analyze it and create a comprehensive trend analysis report. Let me first understand the data structure:

- 327 total questions
- Years: 2015-2025 (11 years, but note: 2020 is missing - likely COVID disruption)
- Types: MCQs, Short, Long
- Question text with `$` delimiters

Let me analyze the data:

**Year distribution:**
- 2015: Questions 1-15 (MCQs), 76-84 (Short), 88, 90, 92, 94 (Long)
- 2016: Questions 94-99 (MCQs), 104, 109, 114, 119, 124, 129, 134, 139, 144, 149, 154, 159, 164, 169 (MCQs), 176-198 (Short), 198, 200, 202 (Long)


- 2017 through 2025: Questions 204-299 (MCQs and Short), 303, 306, 309 (Long), then 312-327 (MCQs), 388-416 (Short), 417, 420, 423 (Long), and continuing through 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 with MCQs, Short, and Long questions interspersed. Now I need to tally up the MCQ counts for each year to identify patterns. I need to recount the entries more systematically by going through the actual data rows rather than trying to piece together the question numbers. Let me trace through what was actually provided for 2016 to get an accurate count instead of relying on potentially incorrect question number sequences. I'm noticing the pattern now—there's a systematic gap of 5 between MCQ entries (like 1, 76, 88, 90, 92, 94) but the subsequent entries shift to 99, 104, 109, 114, 119, 124, 129, 134, 139, 144, 149, 154, 159, 164, 169, which are separated by 5 each. The data appears to have two separate numbering sequences mixed together, and I need to figure out whether the 2015 entries with the 76+ numbering are actually the MCQ set or if something else is going on with how the records are organized.

Let me just work with what I can observe directly rather than trying to reconstruct the full schema. I can see the structure: 2015 has entries starting from 1, then jumping to 76, 88, 90, 92, 94. For 2016, the MCQ entries begin around 94-99, then continue with 104, 109, 114, 119, 124, 129, 134, 139, 144, 149, 154, 159, 164, 169. I should probably write a script to parse this CSV data properly and extract the actual counts per year instead of guessing at the pattern. I'm realizing the gaps in the sequence don't follow a consistent pattern—they might represent deleted records or different question types mixed together. Rather than trying to decode the ID scheme, I should just write a Python script to process the actual CSV data and extract the year and type information directly from each row.

arguments.command:
python3 -c "
import pandas as pd
import re
from collections import Counter

df = pd.read_csv('benchmark/data.csv')

# Topic keyword analysis
# Clean question text - remove delimiters and short tokens
all_text = ' '.join(df['question'].str.lower().tolist())
# Remove \$ delimiters and option text
clean = re.sub(r'\$\s*', ' ', all_text)
clean = re.sub(r'[^a-z\s]', ' ', clean)
words = [w for w in clean.split() if len(w) > 3]
freq = Counter(words)
print('Top 50 keywords:')
for w, c in freq.most_common(50):
    print(f'  {w}: {c}')
"

    curr = yearly.iloc[i]
    yr = yearly.index[i]
    change = curr - prev
    pct = (change / prev) * 100
    print(f'{yr}: {prev} -> {curr} ({change:+d}, {pct:+.1f}%)')

cross = cross.sort_index()

print()

totals = df['type'].value_counts()
total = totals.sum()
for t, c in totals.items():
    print(f'{t}: {c} ({c/total*100:.1f}%)')

print()
print('=== Average per type ===')
for t in ['MCQs','Short','Long']:
    avg = cross[t].mean()
    print(f'{t}: mean={avg:.1f}, min={cross[t].min()}, max={cross[t].max()}')

import pandas as pd
import re
from collections import Counter

df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv')

# === COMPUTE ALL DATA ===
years = sorted(df['year'].unique())
cross = df.groupby(['year','type']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
cross.index = cross.index.astype(int)
cross = cross.sort_index()

# Top keywords
all_text = ' '.join(df['question'].str.lower().tolist())
clean = re.sub(r'\$\s*', ' ', all_text)
clean = re.sub(r'[^a-z\s]', ' ', clean)
words = [w for w in clean.split() if len(w) > 3]
freq = Counter(words)

# Topic classification
def classify_topic(q):
    q = q.lower()
    if any(w in q for w in ['loop', 'for loop', 'while', 'do-while', 'nested', 'iteration', 'continue', 'break']):
        return 'Loops & Iteration'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['switch', 'if', 'else', 'condition', 'nested if', 'decision', '?:', 'ternary']):
        return 'Control Structures'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['operator', 'arithmetic', 'logical', 'increment', 'decrement', 'modulus', 'relational', 'assignment', 'bitwise']):
        return 'Operators & Expressions'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['printf', 'scanf', 'output', 'input', 'format specifier', 'getch', 'gets', 'putchar', 'getche', 'fprintf', 'fscanf', 'fclose', 'fopen']):
        return 'Input/Output Functions'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['function', 'return', 'void', 'parameter', 'recursive', 'recursion', 'user-defined', 'prototype']):
        return 'Functions'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['database', 'dbms', 'rdbms', 'table', 'record', 'field', 'tuple', 'sql', 'dml', 'ddl', 'dcl', 'primary key', 'foreign key', 'relational', 'entity', 'normalization', 'schema', 'acid']):
        return 'Database & DBMS'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['ms-access', 'access', 'form', 'report', 'query', 'macro', 'module']):
        return 'MS Access'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['data type', ' int', 'float', 'char', 'double', 'string', 'variable', 'constant', 'sizeof', 'cast']):
        return 'Data Types & Variables'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['file', 'fopen', 'fclose', 'fprintf', 'fscanf']):
        return 'File Handling'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['algorithm', 'flowchart', 'program', 'compiler', 'interpreter', 'source code', 'object code', 'identifier', 'reserved']):
        return 'Programming Basics'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['array', 'pointer', 'structure', 'union', 'binary search']):
        return 'Advanced Data Structures'
    else:
        return 'Other'

df['topic'] = df['question'].apply(classify_topic)
topic_year = df.groupby(['year','topic']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
topic_year.index = topic_year.index.astype(int)
topic_year = topic_year.sort_index()

# YoY data
yearly_total = df.groupby('year').size().astype(int)
yearly_total.index = yearly_total.index.astype(int)

# Compute percentages per year
pct_data = {}
for yr in cross.index:
    t = cross.loc[yr].sum()
    pct_data[yr] = {
        'MCQs': round(cross.loc[yr,'MCQs']/t*100, 1),
        'Short': round(cross.loc[yr,'Short']/t*100, 1),
        'Long': round(cross.loc[yr,'Long']/t*100, 1),
        'total': t
    }

print("DATA COMPUTED OK")
print("Years:", list(cross.index))
print("Cross:\n", cross)
print("Pct:", pct_data)
PYEOF

python3 << 'PYEOF'
import pandas as pd
import re
from collections import Counter

df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv')

# === COMPUTE ALL DATA ===
years = sorted(df['year'].unique())
cross = df.groupby(['year','type']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
cross.index = cross.index.astype(int)
cross = cross.sort_index()

# Top keywords
all_text = ' '.join(df['question'].str.lower().tolist())
clean = re.sub(r'\$\s*', ' ', all_text)
clean = re.sub(r'[^a-z\s]', ' ', clean)
words = [w for w in clean.split() if len(w) > 3]
freq = Counter(words)

# Topic classification
def classify_topic(q):
    q = q.lower()
    if any(w in q for w in ['loop', 'for loop', 'while', 'do-while', 'nested', 'iteration', 'continue', 'break']):
        return 'Loops & Iteration'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['switch', 'if', 'else', 'condition', 'nested if', 'decision', '?:', 'ternary']):
        return 'Control Structures'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['operator', 'arithmetic', 'logical', 'increment', 'decrement', 'modulus', 'relational', 'assignment', 'bitwise']):
        return 'Operators & Expressions'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['printf', 'scanf', 'output', 'input', 'format specifier', 'getch', 'gets', 'putchar', 'getche', 'fprintf', 'fscanf', 'fclose', 'fopen']):
        return 'Input/Output Functions'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['function', 'return', 'void', 'parameter', 'recursive', 'recursion', 'user-defined', 'prototype']):
        return 'Functions'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['database', 'dbms', 'rdbms', 'table', 'record', 'field', 'tuple', 'sql', 'dml', 'ddl', 'dcl', 'primary key', 'foreign key', 'relational', 'entity', 'normalization', 'schema', 'acid']):
        return 'Database & DBMS'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['ms-access', 'access', 'form', 'report', 'query', 'macro', 'module']):
        return 'MS Access'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['data type', ' int', 'float', 'char', 'double', 'string', 'variable', 'constant', 'sizeof', 'cast']):
        return 'Data Types & Variables'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['file', 'fopen', 'fclose', 'fprintf', 'fscanf']):
        return 'File Handling'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['algorithm', 'flowchart', 'program', 'compiler', 'interpreter', 'source code', 'object code', 'identifier', 'reserved']):
        return 'Programming Basics'
    elif any(w in q for w in ['array', 'pointer', 'structure', 'union', 'binary search']):
        return 'Advanced Data Structures'
    else:
        return 'Other'

df['topic'] = df['question'].apply(classify_topic)
topic_year = df.groupby(['year','topic']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
topic_year.index = topic_year.index.astype(int)
topic_year = topic_year.sort_index()

# YoY data
yearly_total = df.groupby('year').size().astype(int)
yearly_total.index = yearly_total.index.astype(int)

# Compute percentages per year
pct_data = {}
for yr in cross.index:
    t = cross.loc[yr].sum()
    pct_data[yr] = {
        'MCQs': round(cross.loc[yr,'MCQs']/t*100, 1),
        'Short': round(cross.loc[yr,'Short']/t*100, 1),
        'Long': round(cross.loc[yr,'Long']/t*100, 1),
        'total': t
    }

print("DATA COMPUTED OK")
print("Years:", list(cross.index))
print("Cross:\n", cross)
print("Pct:", pct_data)
PYEOF

A comprehensive data-driven examination of question type distributions, year-over-year structural shifts, and recurring topic patterns across 10 examination years and 327 individual questions.

Dataset: BIEK CS Question Bank (community-compiled) • 327 questions • 10 years • 3 question types • Generated April 2026

1. Dataset & Examination Overview

The dataset comprises 327 individual examination questions drawn from BIEK Computer Science Paper-II (theory) across a spanning period from 2015 to 2025. The Board of Intermediate Education Karachi (BIEK) conducts these HSC Part-2 examinations annually, with a supplementary round occasionally offered.

Key Scope Notes

Two important structural facts must be stated upfront:

  • 2020 is absent — The dataset contains no questions for the 2020 examination year. This almost certainly reflects the cancellation of in-person BIEK examinations during the COVID-19 pandemic. This gap must be factored into any year-over-year trend interpretation.
  • Supplementary vs. annual papers are not distinguished — The dataset does not label whether a question originated from an annual or supplementary examination. Some years may aggregate questions from both paper sessions.

  • MCQs are perfectly invariant: Exactly 15 MCQ questions appear in every single year without exception — the most stable element of the entire exam structure across all 10 years.

5. Strategic Insights for Exam Preparation

The patterns in this dataset, while derived from a single subject's question bank, carry actionable implications for both students and teachers. The insights below are tied directly to observed frequencies and structural facts.

1. MCQs Are a Rock-Solid Bet

Exactly 15 MCQ questions appear every single year without variation. Students should treat MCQ preparation as non-negotiable and can rely on the count being stable. The topics循环 (loops), operators, data types, and database basics appear reliably in MCQ form.

2. Short Questions Carry the Most Weight in Era 3

In the current format (2021–2025), Short Questions make up 45.5% of the paper. With 15 Short Questions per session, students must practise writing concise, accurate definitions and explanations. Topics like "difference between X and Y" and "write a program" are perennial.

3. Focus Revision on Database & DBMS First

Database & DBMS content accounts for 19.6% of all questions — the single largest topic block. Key sub-topics include: primary/foreign key distinctions, DML vs. DDL vs. DCL, relational model characteristics, and MS Access objects. These appear across MCQ, Short, and Long formats.

4. Loops + Control Structures Together Dominate

Combining Loops (12.2%) and Control Structures (17.1%) yields nearly 30% of all questions. The while/for/do-while triumvirate and if/switch branching are the most tested programming concepts. Nested loops, break/continue distinctions, and loop-output prediction questions appear regularly in Short format.

5. Three Long Questions — Three Fixed Themes

Long Question 3 consistently covers loops and/or control structures; Question 4 covers operators, I/O functions, or database models; Question 5 covers functions or MS Access objects. This three-part structure has remained consistent across all eras. Teachers can use this as a reliable framework for extended-answer practice.

6. Program-Writing Is a Recurring Short Question Theme

Short Questions requesting C program code appear in nearly every year's Short section (radius/area, swapping, tables, factorial, series). The printf/scanf syntax and loop constructs are essential building blocks for these responses.

7. Emerging Topics: Pointers, Structures, Normalization

Advanced topics such as pointers, structures, and normalization appear only in the 2022 and 2025 papers. This may signal a curriculum expansion in the current era. Students should not neglect these newer additions despite their historically low frequency.

8. Expect No Major Format Changes

The exam has maintained structural stability from 2021 onwards (33 questions, 15 MCQ + 15 Short + 3 Long). Given this five-year stability, the current format is likely to persist. Teachers can confidently plan around the Era 3 structure for upcoming examination cycles.

6. Conclusions & Limitations

Key Findings Summary

  • The BIEK Computer Science exam has not remained structurally stable — it has undergone two distinct structural transitions (2017 expansion, 2021 contraction).
  • MCQs are perfectly stable at 15 per year — the most reliable element of the paper. Long Questions are equally fixed at 3 per year.
  • Short Questions are the sole variable in the exam structure, accounting for all year-to-year volume changes (9 → 18 → 15).
  • The current format (2021–2025) appears fully stabilised at 33 questions with an MCQ/Short/Long split of 15/15/3.
  • Database & DBMS is the single most-tested topic area (19.6%), followed by Control Structures (17.1%) and Loops (12.2%).
  • Advanced topics such as File Handling, Pointers, and Structures appear very infrequently and may be under-represented in the community-compiled dataset.

Data Limitations

  • 2020 missing entirely: No data exists for the 2020 examination year. Any trend line spanning 2019→2021 has a gap that cannot be interpolated with confidence.
  • No annual/supplementary distinction: The dataset does not label papers as annual or supplementary. Some year counts may combine two paper sessions.
  • Community-compiled source: While the dataset is typed and verified, it is not an official BIEK publication. Minor transcription errors in question text are possible.
  • Compact size: With only 327 data points, fine-grained statistical tests (e.g., detecting subtle topic shifts) have limited power. Patterns should be interpreted as directional indicators rather than statistically validated findings.
  • Paper scope: The dataset covers only Paper-II (theory). Practical questions and Paper-I content are excluded unless they overlap with Paper-II topics.

Long Question 3 consistently covers loops and/or control structures; Question 4 covers operators, I/O functions, or database models; Question 5 covers functions or MS Access objects. This three-part structure has remained consistent across all eras. Teachers can use this as a reliable framework for extended-answer practice.

6. Program-Writing Is a Recurring Short Question Theme

Short Questions requesting C program code appear in nearly every year's Short section (radius/area, swapping, tables, factorial, series). The printf/scanf syntax and loop constructs are essential building blocks for these responses.

7. Emerging Topics: Pointers, Structures, Normalization

Advanced topics such as pointers, structures, and normalization appear only in the 2022 and 2025 papers. This may signal a curriculum expansion in the current era. Students should not neglect these newer additions despite their historically low frequency.

8. Expect No Major Format Changes

The exam has maintained structural stability from 2021 onwards (33 questions, 15 MCQ + 15 Short + 3 Long). Given this five-year stability, the current format is likely to persist. Teachers can confidently plan around the Era 3 structure for upcoming examination cycles.

6. Conclusions & Limitations

Key Findings Summary

  • The BIEK Computer Science exam has not remained structurally stable — it has undergone two distinct structural transitions (2017 expansion, 2021 contraction).
  • MCQs are perfectly stable at 15 per year — the most reliable element of the paper. Long Questions are equally fixed at 3 per year.
  • Short Questions are the sole variable in the exam structure, accounting for all year-to-year volume changes (9 → 18 → 15).
  • The current format (2021–2025) appears fully stabilised at 33 questions with an MCQ/Short/Long split of 15/15/3.
  • Database & DBMS is the single most-tested topic area (19.6%), followed by Control Structures (17.1%) and Loops (12.2%).
  • Advanced topics such as File Handling, Pointers, and Structures appear very infrequently and may be under-represented in the community-compiled dataset.

Data Limitations

  • 2020 missing entirely: No data exists for the 2020 examination year. Any trend line spanning 2019→2021 has a gap that cannot be interpolated with confidence.
  • No annual/supplementary distinction: The dataset does not label papers as annual or supplementary. Some year counts may combine two paper sessions.
  • Community-compiled source: While the dataset is typed and verified, it is not an official BIEK publication. Minor transcription errors in question text are possible.
  • Compact size: With only 327 data points, fine-grained statistical tests (e.g., detecting subtle topic shifts) have limited power. Patterns should be interpreted as directional indicators rather than statistically validated findings.
  • Paper scope: The dataset covers only Paper-II (theory). Practical questions and Paper-I content are excluded unless they overlap with Paper-II topics.
BIEK Computer Science 12th Class — Trend Analysis Report 2015–2025 • Data source: community-compiled question bank on Kaggle (user: sadamumer) • All figures derived exclusively from data.csv
